title: A campaign outlives its worker
description: A campaign targets 50 million recipients. At 100,000 deliveries/s, expansion and delivery take several minutes. One API request currently loops through everyone; a crash restarts from the beginning, and operators cannot pause it cleanly. What should replace that loop?

options.text: Increase the API request timeout and keep the recipient list in its process memory.
options.explanation: A longer timeout does not preserve progress after a crash or provide a durable place to control the campaign.

options.text: Persist a campaign job, expand recipients in checkpointed chunks, and pace idempotent delivery jobs through channel queues.
options.explanation: Chunk checkpoints make restarts bounded, pacing respects downstream capacity, and persisted campaign state gives operators a pause or cancel control. Deterministic delivery IDs handle replay.

options.text: Fetch all recipients in one database transaction and hold it open until sends finish.
options.explanation: A long transaction ties database resources to external provider work and still cannot make provider calls part of that transaction.

options.text: Give each API instance a copy of the full segment and let instances race to finish it.
options.explanation: Without durable ownership and checkpoints, this duplicates work and increases provider contention rather than making recovery predictable.
